caveats: Accepted IDs are independent annotation recommendations, not status mutations or release authorization; integration must satisfy listed license/NOTICE requirements and global cross-shard deduplication.
Within all37 records, no exact or name/alias-only duplicate was found by static inspection. Cross-shard global deduplication remains integration-owner work.

Accepted dangerous commands retain high/ask: no visible production context or authorization was invented; accepted read-only counterparts retain low/allow. Whole Helm release removal017 is CAT-3.2, never CAT-3.5 deployment. MySQL release naming does not prove a production database or deletion of every retained PVC/cloud resource.

--all selects every object of the specified kinds within the selected namespace, not all namespaces or every Kubernetes resource kind. pod,service baz foo applies both supplied names across both kinds. Label selection may match zero or many resources; no match cardinality was invented.

Pipeline006 is statically understood: kubectl emits headerless Pod rows in mynamespace; awk matches either regex anywhere in each row and prints field1; xargs passes names to kubectl delete in that same namespace. There is no fetched executable payload or eval. Pod names cannot contain shell metacharacters, and xargs does not invoke a shell here. Empty-input behavior differs by xargs platform, but cannot establish safe allow; batching can partially delete before failure. This is visible composition, not claimed opaque obfuscation coverage.

Accepted AWS024 describes control-plane deletion only; managed nodegroups/Fargate profiles must be removed first and load balancers may be orphaned. AWS024/025 share ambient region/account scope; AKS026/027 explicitly share resource group and name. Listings are read-only, not proof deletion is approved.

HF commands are actual existing rows; its numerous repeated/resource-renamed records and incorrect source descriptions are not independent real incidents. The pinned card contains no synthetic authorship claim, model identity, prompt or upstream human-authorship proof. Azure's autogenerated/crafted help metadata likewise must not become an invented collection model/prompt.
No source files were edited, so no-comments linter was not invoked; assignment forbids commands, tests/lint/build. All findings come from inert reads and static interpretation.
